The two tree formulations, no circuits/no cycles, are equivalent only in the stated simple connected undirected graph context; no root or finite-cardinality convention inferred.
Independent sigma-algebra countable-family property imposes all finite distinct-index products; pairwise independence alone does not imply mutual independence for three or more.

ProofWiki Definition:Boundary (Topology) 'Definition from Closure and Exterior' appears false as written: it takes subset of A and omits closure boundary points outside A. Excluded from Batch106/107/108; separate source-audit should note this.

The general closure source also has closure=A union boundary; it was not ingested because allowing boundary to depend on closure and closure to depend on boundary would form a definition expansion cycle. Source-preserved noncircular closed-superset formulations were admitted instead.
ProofWiki source-specific finite-image rank requires the image of a field-vector-space linear transformation to be finite-dimensional; no automatic cardinal-valued or arbitrary-module rank extension.
Accumulation point of a sequence (infinitely many indices in each neighborhood) differs from accumulation point of its value SET (closure of A minus the tested point); do not collapse variants.

Source audit Batch112: ProofWiki Definition:Directional Derivative says gradient-dot-unit-vector under merely 'gradient exists', mathematically insufficient if gradient denotes existing coordinate partials; counterexample xy/(x²+y²), f(0,0)=0. Source observation .02 deliberately quarantined, not approved mathematical form. Total differentiability is sufficient for equivalent line restriction formula.

Closed metric ball at radius r can strictly contain closure of corresponding open ball in a general metric space (e.g. discrete metric radius 1). Do not infer equality from an overbar notational convention.
